original_question: Can one develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-type interacting-particle models that plays a role analogous to KAM theory in integrable dynamical systems, so that persistence of integrability-like structure and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena can be studied beyond exactly solvable models?
target_in_paper: Problem 3 (interacting particle systems and KPZ), specifically the closing informal open problem asking for a perturbation theory, analogous to KAM theory, for non-solvable models in the KPZ/interacting-particle-systems setting. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the paper’s distinctive core idea very well: the missing tool is a perturbation theory explicitly compared to KAM theory; the goal is to treat non-solvable models rather than only exactly solvable/integrable ones; and the purpose is to study persistence of integrability-like structure together with robustness of asymptotic scaling behavior. That is essentially the paper’s final open problem in Problem 3. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
missing_details: The paper places this problem specifically inside Problem 3, i.e. the KPZ/interacting-particle-systems discussion, not as a general question about integrable systems in all contexts. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The surrounding motivation is that, aside from a few exceptions, rigorous asymptotic scaling results for KPZ/interacting particle systems had mostly been obtained only for restricted classes of initial data; that context is part of why the perturbation-theory question is being asked. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The paper does not formalize a model class, perturbation size, topology, or notion of closeness; your draft implicitly sounds more formal than the source, which leaves these choices open. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The source deliberately puts "integrability" in quotation marks, signaling that the issue is persistence of the solvability structures behind exact asymptotic analysis, not a formally defined Liouville-integrability condition. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The relevant asymptotic phenomena in the nearby discussion are KPZ-type scaling behaviors, especially 3:2:1 scaling and related fluctuation/correlation limits, rather than arbitrary scaling phenomena. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The paper is informal here: it gives no quantifiers, no theorem-style hypotheses/conclusions, no operator definitions, and no algebraic data such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree bounds, or nilpotency conditions; those items are simply not part of this problem’s formulation. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
refined_question: Within the KPZ/interacting-particle-systems setting, can one develop a perturbation theory, analogous to KAM theory for integrable dynamical systems, that applies to non-solvable models and can be used to investigate the persistence of the paper’s quoted "integrability" and to demonstrate the robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena, in particular beyond the exactly solvable examples and the restricted initial-data regimes for which rigorous results are presently known? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the last open problem stated in Problem 3, not the earlier but separate question about proving strong 3:2:1 KPZ universality for the KPZ equation itself. The giveaway is the near-verbatim KAM analogy: Deift says there is no known perturbation theory analogous to KAM that would allow one to study persistence of "integrability" for non-solvable models and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena. The immediately preceding context explains that this is being posed after a review of integrable KPZ/interacting-particle models, ASEP, the strong KPZ-universality question, and the limitation to restricted initial data. The paper offers this as an informal open problem rather than as a numbered conjecture or theorem, so the refined version should stay narrow and contextual rather than invent formal hypotheses the paper does not supply. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
